title: Portal reseller statements
description: What a reseller owes Fugaro for one month (portal plan P6.3; D2189, D2190). The direction is the finding: resellers owe Fugaro and there are no commissions. A statement is the month's accrual — days times seats times the wholesale rate — with one line per customer, issued once by an idempotent run and then read; what is paid against it is recorded here by operations and by nobody else, because only a person sees the money arrive. Every object here is closed, because ee/keyservice/wire_statements.go decodes it with DisallowUnknownFields.

statement.description: One reseller's month, as the reseller and the operations team read it.

id.description: The statement's id. A run of a month that has already been issued returns the statement that exists rather than making a second (P6.3's TestStatementRunIsIdempotent), so this is what a payment is recorded against.

reseller_organisation_id.description: The reseller that owes the money — the organisation the statement is addressed to and not the customers', which are its lines.

month.description: The month the accrual is for, as `YYYY-MM` in UTC. A month boundary is a time zone's opinion, and a boundary that followed the reader's clock would put one day's accrual in two statements.

accrued_micros.description: What the month's accrual came to, in micro-dollars. It is the sum of the lines, and it is what the credit limit was measured against while the month ran.

paid_micros.description: What has been recorded against it so far, in micro-dollars. It is kept beside the accrual rather than netted off it: a statement is issued before it is paid, and a partly paid one has to keep saying what it was for.

state.description: Open or paid, and it follows the two amounts: a statement whose payments cover its accrual is paid, so no separate act closes one and no run can leave one open that was settled.

lines.description: One entry per customer the month accrued for. The order is stable, so a reseller comparing two months can see which customer moved.

issued_at.description: When the statement was issued, in UTC — the run's instant, which is after the month it covers.

paid_at.description: When the last payment settled it, in UTC, or null while it is open. A partial payment leaves this null and moves paid_micros.

line.description: One customer's part of a statement.

organisation_id.description: The customer organisation the accrual was for, linked to the reseller through the link operations sets (P6.1).

amount_micros.description: That customer's accrual for the month, in micro-dollars. It is not signed: a revoked entitlement stops accruing rather than crediting, and a correction is a payment recorded against the statement.

payment.description: Operations' record that money arrived against one statement (P6.3's TestPaymentIsRecordedByOperationsOnly). The statement it is for is the route's own target and not a field, so a payment cannot be recorded against two.

amount_micros.description: What was received, in micro-dollars, and it may be less than the statement: a partial payment leaves it open and shows both figures. It must be more than nothing — a payment of zero is a mistake and not a fact.

paid_at.description: When the money arrived, in UTC, which is the bank's date and not the day somebody typed it in.

reference.description: The bank or transfer reference operations was given, kept so that a payment can be matched to a statement months later — and so that the same transfer entered twice is visible as the same reference.
